jina: Provisions concerning appointment to offices in the public service
maudhui: (1) For the purposes of interpreting the provisions of this Constitution concerning the procedure for appointment to offices in the service of the Government of the United Republic, it is hereby declared that any person who, pursuant to the provisions of this Constitution, has power to appoint or elect another person to hold a certain office, also has power to appoint or elect a person to act in or temporarily hold and perform the functions of that office: Provided that the provisions of this subarticle shall not apply to the offices of Minister, Deputy Minister, Justice of Appeal, Judge of the High Court, member of the Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance or member of the Electoral Commission. (2) The following rules shall also apply for the purposes of interpreting the provisions of this Constitution concerning the procedure for appointment to offices in the service of the Government of the United Republic— (a) where a person holding an office established by this Constitution is on leave pending relinquishment of that office, another person may be appointed to that office notwithstanding that the first-mentioned person is still holding that office; (b) where two or more persons are concurrently holding the same office by reason of an appointment made pursuant to paragraph (a) of this subarticle, then in any case where any function connected with that office is required to be performed, the person most recently appointed shall be deemed to be the sole holder of that office; and (c) where a person has been appointed pursuant to the provisions of this Constitution to act in or hold an office while the substantive holder of that office is unable to perform the functions of that office, the validity of the appointment of the person so appointed shall not be questioned on the ground that the substantive holder was not unable to perform the functions of that office.
